newsitem.title: UK: Tories "Demon Eyes" poster sparks most talk in '96.
newsitem.headline: Tories "Demon Eyes" poster sparks most talk in '96.

text.p: The Conservative Party's "demon eyes" poster campaign sparked more press coverage in Britain than any other advertisement over the last three years, according to a survey released on Wednesday.

The controversial poster ad run by the Tories last summer -- which featured Labour leader Tony Blair shown with demon-like red eyes peering out from behind a curtain -- beat out Wonderbra poster ads displaying the charms of buxom models Eva Herzigova and Caprice Bourret to become Britain's most-talked about ad, Propeller Marketing Communications said.
The "demon eyes" poster ad, which was headlined "New Labour, New Danger," topped Propeller Marketing's poll of 1996 Ads That Make the News.

"The Tory campaign generated more than twice the number of stories about Wonderbra, which was previously the most talked about ad," said Martin Loat, managing director Propeller Marketing. "And it made nearly four times the number of stories about the Labour campaign.
"Like it or loathe it, the Demon eyes icon was a stunning advertising image that captured the public imagination," Loat said.
The Tory ad campaign, which also featured the "Honest John" posters showing Prime Minister John Major's eyes, generated 126 press stories in 1996.
Campaign, an advertising trade publication, earlier this month named the "Demon Eyes" poster the top UK ad for 1996.

The Wonderbra ads with models Herzigova and Bourret garnered 51 news stories in 1996, making it the second most-talked about ad. In third place was British Telecommunications Plc for the "It's Good to Talk" campaign with 48 news stories.
